newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TranzRail sees Q4 freight hit by slow NZ economy.
newsitem.headline: TranzRail sees Q4 freight hit by slow NZ economy.

text.p: New Zealand rail operator Tranz Rail Holdings Ltd said on Thursday its freight volumes carried to date in the fourth quarter since April 1 had unexpectedly dipped and would likely reduce earnings.

In comments alongside its results for the three months to March 31, the company, whose largest owner is U.S. rail freight group Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp, said it saw pronounced weakness in the coal and forestry products trades.
"Tranz Link (bulk freight) volumes carried to date in the fourth quarter of this financial year have unexpectedly dipped below prior year and prior period (third quarter) levels," the company said.

"Softness in South Island export coal tonnages, weaker trading across all segments of the New Zealand forest products sector, combined with the overall slower trading in the domestic economy will likely reduce earnings for the quarter," it added.

The company reported an NZ$6.2 million rise in its third quarter net profit to $20.6 million ($14.2 million), or 16 cents per share, saying reduced interest costs and operating cost cuts were the main drivers.

Freight and passenger revenue for the quarter was $145.9 million, up slightly on the year-ago quarter and assisted by a seven percent rise in Interislander seaborne passenger and vehicle revenue, as well as a four percent increase in rail passnger revenue. (1US$=1.449 NZ$)
